checks: The original G is a sheaf on arbitrary X. Restriction along the actual open immersion evaluates the same G on image opens; the image/preimage adjunction proves finality in the actual restriction direction.

Every semilocal/local/fiber-product value is an actual scheme-neighborhood colimit. The general restriction and overlap arrows are induced by actual local-scheme morphisms and pullback projections, and commute with the chart comparisons on representatives.

The finite family only has to exhaust actual closed points of S. The general theorem does not require X affine, ambient selected points closed, local schemes open, or the extended presheaf already known to be a sheaf.

generalFinitePointValueIso and its naturality identify the actual original-X convention on j image sigma and the original natural map. The affine chart presents the given semilocalization; no unproved quasi-projective library theorem is claimed.

The explicit non-open example lives in the actual two-rational-point semilocalization of Spec Q[X][Y]. The chosen point is proved closed there; the actual map localToSemilocal has non-open image, hence is not an open immersion.

The non-open proof uses the full infinite family ker(Y-aX): each prime lies below the first selected maximal ideal but not below the second. A basic open inside the putative local image forces its defining polynomial into all these kernels; infinitely many distinct roots force it to zero. Smoothness, affineness and integrality of the original plane are proved.

checks: The imported Cor category consists of actual signed finite-correspondence cycles with componentwise diagonals and incidence-Tor composition on smooth separated finite-type schemes. PresheafWithTransfers is the actual additive opposite functor to abelian groups; its A1 condition is the stated projection isomorphism. Its irreducible source components coincide with connected components on the smooth models by the proved clopen integral-component geometry.

SmoothZariski.topology is proved equal to the topology generated by actual jointly covering open immersions. Its comparison with Nisnevich is only an inclusion of topologies; the original canonical Zariski unit is never replaced by the Nisnevich unit.

S5ZariskiKernel proves that a section killed by the genuine Nisnevich unit is Zariski-locally zero, by an integral affine cover, actual generic splitting of a Nisnevich covering sieve, and the existing all-field original-presheaf local-zero theorem. Conversely the genuine Nisnevich sheaf kills such locally zero sections. No simultaneous finite-point conclusion is inferred from these individual point witnesses.

The native Nisnevich image is identified with the literal quotient by the Zariski-zero subgroup using its actual kernel and pointwise epimorphism. Its transfer action and HI are inherited from proved native structures. This is a proved auxiliary identification, not an assumed transfer structure on an arbitrary ordinary sheafification.

The canonical Zariski-to-Nisnevich comparison is sheafifyLift of the original unit; its exact unit equation is proved. Its pointwise injectivity follows from the proved Zariski local injectivity, rather than an assumed separatedness of the original F.

The finite-point geometry produces one actual common Cor/A1 moving factor. In the infinite-field branch the simultaneous parameter product, whole-fibre smooth neighborhood, retained boundary and finite boundary frames preserve all prescribed auxiliary closed points. The extension to nonclosed original points is proved by choosing closed specializations and using generization-stability of opens.

The finite-field branch forms all polynomial avoidance conditions over the original base, chooses two sufficiently large separable extensions of coprime positive degrees, and retains the full inverse image of every auxiliary point. The domain condition after scalar extension is proved using degree coprimality at one actual closed point; geometric integrality is not added.

The finite scalar descent removes finite closed images of the bad complements to obtain one original-base neighborhood. The actual transpose trace followed by a moving correspondence yields degree times original restriction. Signed integer Bezout coefficients combine the two factors. The correspondence beta is chosen before quantifying over HI presheaves, so precisely the same beta acts on F and its genuine HI Nisnevich sheafification; no scalar-zero or scalar-lift hypothesis is substituted.

The zero-dimensional branch proves that the smooth affine domain is a field and that a nonempty open immersion is an isomorphism. Finite or infinite and zero or positive dimensional case splits cover every field and smooth integral affine model. IntegralAffineMoving is an intermediate predicate proved by integralAffineMoving_of_field, not a hypothesis of the final endpoint.

For kernel vanishing, an actual zero representative exists on a nonempty affine open, and the one common transfer factor kills the restriction on a neighborhood of the whole finite set. For surjectivity, a Zariski sheaf section has an original representative on a nonempty affine open; transfer naturality, proved HI of genuine Nisnevich sheafification, and injectivity of the canonical comparison establish the required equality in actual Zariski sheafification.

For nonintegral affine X, smoothness gives finitely many pairwise disjoint clopen integral components. Each component is proved affine. Their shrunk opens combine to an actual open immersion into the original X. The original F sections assemble by actual finite-correspondence biproduct identities, without any sheaf assumption on F; only the true Zariski sheaf is used for uniqueness.

The ambient adapter uses the affine neighborhood W already selected in the task. Inside each original neighborhood U it constructs an affine neighborhood in U intersect W retaining the entire original finite set, then transports geometric open immersions through their actual open images. It neither requires ambient X affine or quasi-affine nor replaces the original neighborhood category.

The literal all-open-neighborhood colimit is filtered in the shrinking direction. Its representatives and equality-after-common-shrink are proved for actual abelian-group colimits. The simultaneous zero and lift producers are instantiated on every original neighborhood; pointwise stalk equality alone is never used as semilocal equality.

S5Complete.semilocal_zariski_unit_isIso concludes IsIso of the actual siteNeighborhoodUnit with only Field k, P.IsA1Invariant, original smooth X, a finite nonempty original set, and its task-selected affine W. All geometric, representative, separation and gluing hypotheses of intermediate helpers are discharged.

The final small-site theorem uses the proved continuous and cocontinuous opens functor and the exact restrictionIso_unit and neighborhoodRestrictionIso_unit identities. Thus it proves the same canonical ordinary small-Zariski sheafification unit on the same original-X colimit, not just an unrelated arrow between isomorphic groups.

The final proof is a direct common-correspondence reconstruction. The older SingletonBlockGluing and successful binary-shrinking helpers remain conditional auxiliary results; the endpoint does not assume them or claim to have separately proved every stronger unshrunk Mayer-Vietoris assertion.
